methods.label: Separate positive and negative inputs
methods.explanation:
The value of \(|x|\) depends on the sign of \(x\), so consider the two possible signs. The condition \(x\ne0\) ensures that the denominator is nonzero.

If \(x>0\), then \(|x|=x\), giving
\[
\frac{|x-|x||}{x}=\frac{|x-x|}{x}=0.
\]
If \(x<0\), then \(|x|=-x\). Thus \(x-|x|=2x<0\), whose absolute value is \(-2x\). Hence
\[
\frac{|x-|x||}{x}=\frac{-2x}{x}=-2.
\]
These cases exhaust all nonzero real numbers. Neither \(0\) nor \(-2\) is a positive integer, so there are no qualifying values of \(x\). The answer is choice E.
methods.levelReason: The method applies the elementary absolute-value rule separately to positive and negative inputs and checks both resulting values.
